sentences.text:
This first bail application under Section 438 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 is filed on behalf of the applicant Manish Yadav S/o Shri Udaybhan Singh Yadav, for grant of anticipatory bail, who is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.229/2023 registered at Police Station - Hanumanganj, District Bhopal (MP) for offence punishable under Sections 376, 376(2)(n), 323, 506 and 34 of IPC.
2.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is submitted by learned counsel for applicant that FIR was lodged on 12.04.2023.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text: Incident allegedly took place starting from 2016.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is submitted that after 7 years, FIR was lodged.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text: Prosecutrix always knew that applicant was a married person.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text: Since he is a police personnel, he is being blackmailed.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Earlier complainant/prosecutrix had lodged case at Crime No.0334/2021 at Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178619517/
1

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text: Police Station Teelajamalpura, under Section 354, 341, 294, 323, 506 and 34 of IPC against two other persons
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text: . In this case, final report was submitted by police declaring the case to be a false and concocted one.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text: Placing reliance on this material, it is submitted that prosecutrix is in habit of making false allegations.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text: 3. Placing reliance on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case o f Naim Ahmed Vs. State (NCT of Delhi) 2023 SCC OnLine SC 89 and from reading paragraphs 20 and 21, it is pointed out that Hon'ble Supreme Court has made a distinction between giving a false promise and committing breach of promise by the accused and case of breach of promise.

entities.text: f Naim Ahmed Vs. State (NCT of Delhi) 2023 SCC OnLine SC 89
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text:
It is submitted that in the case of false promise, the accused right from the beginning would not have any intention to marry the prosecutrix whereas in case of breach of promise one cannot deny the possibility that the accused might have given a promise with all seriousness to marry her and subsequently might have encountered certain circumstances unforeseen by him or the circumstances beyond his control,
which prevented him to fulfill his promise.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text: 4. Reading from the said judgment, it is submitted that since the prosecutrix knew that applicant was married, there is no question of any false promise and, therefore, it is a case of consent.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Thus,
applicant is entitled to grant anticipatory bail, looking to the fact that he is a police personnel.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text: 5. Shri Vivek Lakhera, learned Government Advocate in his turn submits that case is slightly different.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is not like that the prosecutrix knew from the beginning that applicant is married.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text: Applicant was exploiting her since 2016 in the name of marriage.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text: They were in relationship.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text: When prosecutrix became pregnant, she asked the applicant to marry her.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text: When applicant forced her to undergo abortion and that is the time she came to know of the fact that applicant is already married.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text: Reading from statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., it is submitted that the prosecutrix has supported the case of prosecution has given statement against the applicant.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text: 6. Shri Dharmendra Patel, learned counsel for complainant also submits that it is not a case of breach of promise but that of a false promise as the prosecutrix was not knowing the status of applicant to be a married man from the beginning.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text: She discovered it later on when the applicant had promised her to divorce his wife and continued to indulge in relationship.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text: 7. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, facts in the case of Naim Ahmed (supra) are different.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text: It has come on record that prosecutrix therein was a married woman having three children and under those facts and circumstances, Hon'ble Supreme Court noted a fact that prosecutrix could not have been under misconception of fact by giving consent to have sexual relationship with the appellant.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text: Hon'ble Supreme Court specifically noted a fact that the prosectrix being a married woman and mother of three children was matured and intelligent enough to understand the significance and consequences of the moral or immoral quality of acts she was consenting to.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text: However, in the present case though Shri Ajay Gupta, Senior Advocate submits that prosecutrix knew from the beginning that applicant was married but from the statement given by the prosecutrix under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., this fact is not corroborated.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is a matter of investigation and for the present, it is not a case to show indulgence in the matter of grant of anticipatory bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Applicant is in detention since 03.05.2024.
2.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 July, 2024.json

sentences.text: As per the prosecution story, allegation against the present applicant and other co-accused persons is of kidnapping the prosecutrix and committing sexual intercourse with her.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 July, 2024.json

sentences.text: On the basis of said allegation, police registered the case against the present applicant under the aforesaid sections.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 July, 2024.json

sentences.text: 3 . Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant is in custody since 03.05.2024 and he has falsely been implicated in this case.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 July, 2024.json

sentences.text: Age of the prosecutrix is 17 years, 10 months and 17 days on the date of incident.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 July, 2024.json

sentences.text: No sexual assault has been caused by the present applicant.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 July, 2024.json

sentences.text: It is further submitted 2 MCRC-28803-2024 that name of the applicant is not mentioned in the FIR, but later on, in the statements of prosecutrix recorded u/Ss.161 and 164 of Cr.P.C., name of applicant is mentioned.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 July, 2024.json

sentences.text: Charge sheet has been filed.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 July, 2024.json

sentences.text: There is no criminal history of the applicant.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 July, 2024.json

sentences.text: Therefore, it is prayed that the applicant may be released on bail pending the trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 July, 2024.json

sentences.text: 4 . O n the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the grant of bail to the applicant on the ground that prosecutrix in her statements recorded u/Ss.161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. has stated that present applicant has first committed rape with the prosecutrix thereafter he alongwith other co-accused persons kidnapped her at night and thereafter the present applicant took her to the Bangalore.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 July, 2024.json

sentences.text: Therefore, he prayed for dismissal of this bail application.
sentences._hearing_file: Manish Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 July, 2024.json

sentences.text: 5. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case as well as looking to the seriousness of offence, it is not a fit case to release the applicant on bail.

applicant is entitled to grant anticipatory bail, looking to the fact that he is a police personnel.
Applicant was exploiting her since 2016 in the name of marriage.

When prosecutrix became pregnant, she asked the applicant to marry her.
